title: fix step answer
description: One entry per blocker: the change, and the test that goes red when the blocker comes back. A blocker cleared without a test is a blocker that can return unnoticed.

skills.description: Every Superpowers skill invoked in this step. The driver cross-checks this against the Skill calls in the run log, so a claim here the log does not show is a failed step.

redWhen.description: The production change that makes this test fail — the fix deleted, not a typo introduced. A test whose author cannot name one is measuring the shape of the code.

testCommit.description: The commit that added the test, seven characters or more. The driver re-runs that test at the change's parent and at the change, so this and implCommit are what make failedBefore checkable rather than claimed.

implCommit.description: The commit that made it pass. It must not be testCommit: one squashed commit cannot show which came first.

deferred.description: A finding that is not a blocker, with where it went. A deferral with no follow-up is a finding dropped.

question.description: Why this step cannot finish. Answerable in a line: a yes/no or a pick.

questionKind.description: What kind of question it is. `base-red`: a red that fails the same way at the merge base. `uncommitted-fix`: the change passes but is not committed. `already-fixed`: the ask already holds on the integration branch. `uat-data`: it wants UAT or production data. `other`: anything else. Never ask for UAT or production data: measure on the local seed or the fixtures, and say so in the pull request.

questionFor.description: Who answers the question. `owner`: pixels, a picture, a product or commercial call, or the data model. `pm`: the ticket's shape — which repo, how it splits, the order, the wording of its acceptance. Unsure is `owner`; the driver treats anything but `pm` as the owner's.

replacedTests.description: Every test file in which this step removed, reworded or skipped an it()/test() case. `file` is the repo-relative path exactly as git shows it. Give exactly one of `coveredBy` — a bare repo-relative path, nothing else, to the test file at head that now pins the same behaviour (the same file, for a reworded case) — or `removedBecause`, one line on why the behaviour is gone. The ship step writes these into the pull request's `## Deleted tests` section, and the deleted-tests gate checks each line. Empty when no case was removed, reworded or skipped.

gateFixes.description: One entry per GATE finding (an id starting gate-): a self-check gate this project runs went red, and this is the commit that repairs it. There is no red/green test for a compile or lint error — the proof is the driver re-running every gate straight after this step, and nothing is pushed past a red one.

commit.description: The commit that repairs the gate, seven characters or more. It must be on the branch.

pmProofs.description: A blocking finding a `## PM answer` on the ticket names and accepts a non-test proof for, answered without a red/green pair. `kind: mutation` (the answer accepts a mutation proof, for a test-only or type-only finding): the driver plants `break` in the fixed code at `commit`, runs `command` and requires it to FAIL, restores the code and requires it to PASS. `kind: commit` (the answer accepts the fixing commit, for a doc- or wording-only finding): the driver checks `commit` is the one the answer names, is on the branch, and touches the file the finding names. Never used without such an answer.

pmAnswer.description: The `ref` of the PM answer that accepts this proof, exactly as the brief lists it.

commit.description: mutation: the commit holding the fix, where the break is planted. commit: the fixing commit the PM answer names. Seven characters or more, on the branch.

testFile.description: mutation: the test (or the file the type check covers) the command runs.

command.description: mutation: the named test or type check, run in the tree at commit.

break.description: mutation: a literal find/replace in the fixed code, never in testFile, that the command must go red on.

autoProofs.description: A blocking finding no red/green pair can show, fixed by a commit that is only docs, only comments, only wording, or only tests — answered with no PM answer, because the driver checks the class itself (scripts/proof-class.py, off the commit's diff, for the kinds proof.autoAccept turns on). docs-only: every file the commit touches is docs. comment-only: every changed code line is a comment or blank. wording-only: the code differs only inside string literals or JSX text. test-only: every file is a test, and `break` is a literal find/replace in NON-test code that the driver plants at `commit`; `command` must FAIL with it and PASS once the code is restored. A claim the diff does not bear out is refused.

commit.description: The one commit holding the fix, on the branch, touching the file the finding names. Seven characters or more.

testFile.description: test-only: the test the fix changed, which the command runs.

command.description: test-only: the command that runs testFile, in the tree at commit.

break.description: test-only: a literal find/replace in the code the test pins — never in a test file — that the command must go red on.

bodyProofs.description: A blocking finding about the PR description, or a check that reads it (an approved picture, a ## Lesson section, evidence routes), cleared by editing the description rather than by a commit. Name the repo's own check: the driver fetches the description from GitHub itself, runs `command` in the worktree with BODY_FILE set to the description and LABELS to the PR's labels, the branch's changed paths on stdin, and requires it to exit 0 on the description now and to fail on the description as it stood when the review judged it. Your own run of it is not evidence.

command.description: The check that reads the description, run from the worktree root, e.g. `sh scripts/check-approved-mock/index.sh`.

gitActions.description: Git steps your permission mode refuses, which the driver checks and runs after this answer, in order: commitMerge stages the resolved conflicted paths and finishes the merge in progress with --no-edit; resetTo moves the branch to sha, one of its own commits not on the trunk or its head on origin; dropLocalCommits resets the branch to origin when every local commit is already there. One refused stops the rest.
